speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of a second instance of assault at a place of worship in less than half a year (a) how does the Ministry plan to strengthen collaboration between religious institutions, their surrounding communities and security agencies to enhance the early detection and prevention of potential security threats; and (b) whether the Ministry has plans to take additional steps to provide further assurance to the public of their personal safety at places of worship.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the rise of extremist threats, whether our schools, places of worship, hospitals and public institutions are being prepared to respond to potential terrorist attacks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MHA also works closely with the Ministry of Education (MOE) on crisis preparedness in schools.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Such exercises and drills familiarise school staff and students with emergency situations and facilitate collaboration between the schools and emergency responders during a crisis.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MOH maintains close communication with healthcare institutions to uphold security postures and implement security enhancement programmes in partnership with the Police.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They will also engage the relevant stakeholders to step up security measures.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At some point, I hope never, but we have to be prepared that an attack will succeed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And when it does, it is important that, as a community, we remain resilient and united.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This requires us to be physically and psychologically prepared.
